title: The Slow Machine
premise: Marguerite Thackeray, sole caretaker of Earth's abandoned seed vault, ferries supplies along a trade route between two colonies that severed contact after a war neither will explain. When she intercepts a distress call in a language extinct for two centuries, she discovers both fleets are secretly descendants of the same lost ship — and that Earth's final transmission loop, still broadcasting an old lie to keep them apart, is about to end. To prevent mutual annihilation when the loop dies and the truth surfaces uncontrolled, Marguerite must keep the lie alive long enough to deliver it herself, on her own terms. In the end she sacrifices her identity as Earth's last voice, revealing the shared origin of both peoples and choosing truth over the loyalty that once defined her.
about_author: Noor Crane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete broadcast records before turning to fiction. They write slow-burning science fiction about people who maintain machines meant to outlast them.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She runs her supply circuit between the rival colonies of Vesper and Calloway, trading carefully, speaking to each about the other in lies she was trained to tell. The seed vault's AI, Root, nags her about Earth's dying transmission loop. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking dread.

chapters.title: A Language Without Speakers
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A distress signal arrives in Pre-Diaspora English, extinct for two centuries, leading her to a derelict ship whose logs reveal both colonies descend from one lost vessel — the very fact Earth's transmission loop was built to bury. A Vesper patrol nearly catches her. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear as loyalty and truth begin to split.

chapters.title: The Loop Ends
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Root and intercepted fleet channels. The transmission loop fails early; fragments of the old lie leak to both fleets, which mobilize toward the vault believing the other side caused it. Marguerite must decide whether to repair the lie or break it. Climax: she broadcasts the derelict's logs in the dead language, forcing both fleets to hear their common mother tongue. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Seeds Remember
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, months later. The fleets stand down, uneasy but bound by shared grief; envoys meet aboard the derelict. Marguerite plants the recovered seeds in open ground for the first time, no longer Earth's caretaker but something new. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace — identity rebuilt from chosen truth rather than inherited duty.
